brief:
Small-scale agricultural projects are offering lifelines to Gaza farmers struggling to rebuild after widespread destruction, Al Jazeera English reported. Greenhouses and rented plots enable cultivators to grow crops despite the extensive devastation across the territory, providing economic stability for families attempting to restore their means of survival and income.

The initiatives represent practical efforts by farmers to resume production on limited available land, adapting farming methods to current conditions rather than awaiting large-scale reconstruction efforts. Agricultural workers are deploying these modest-scale operations to maintain food production and generate revenue while the broader recovery process unfolds in Gaza.
dek: Greenhouses and rented plots are lifelines for Gaza farmers, helping them grow crops despite the extensive destruction.
title: Gaza farmers rebuild livelihoods through small-scale cultivation projects.
